subject: Authbroker time-sync regression causing short control-plane disconnects
messages:
From: Cheng Li <cheng@medsyn.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Cc: support@medsyn.com
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Brief: control-plane blips after kernel sync on edge nodes

Hi Michael,

We're seeing repeated short (30-90s) control-plane connection drops from our private deploy starting ~09:50 PDT after our nightly kernel sync on our edge fleet. The Redwood agent briefly loses auth and recovers; regen of sessions seems automatic but it's impacting user requests.

Attached is a small diagnostic bundle with connection traces and agent logs for the affected window (diag_dump_20270515.tgz). We're hoping to understand whether this aligns with the auto-update you mentioned in your last runbook or if something in our environment triggered a token validation regression.

Can your team confirm whether there were any management-plane changes or a known regression in the authbroker around that time? We can open a bridge if helpful — prefer daytime window tomorrow if a rollback is needed.

Thanks,
Cheng Li
SRE, Medsyn Health
attachments: diag_dump_20270515.tgz

Immediate asks:

If this looks like the authbroker regression we observed in canary last month, Rishi and I will propose a rollback plan and an evidence packet for your procurement team.

I can host a quick bridge this afternoon if helpful — but if you prefer a controlled maintenance window, we can schedule a 1h rollback overnight to minimize impact.

-mg

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Cheng Li <cheng@medsyn.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 12:20:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Brief: control-plane blips after kernel sync on edge nodes

Cheng / team — I've ingested the diagnostic bundle and correlated it with our authbroker telemetry. Quick summary:

- Root cause (prelim): a time-sync edge case in authbroker v1.4.2 where clock drift > 250ms causes token validation to fail transiently during keepalive handshakes. The condition was triggered by an upstream chrony update on your nodes.
- Manifestation: agent disconnect + automatic session re-negotiation (30–90s impact window), no data loss but increased request latency and retry churn.
- Repro steps: can reproduce in our lab by forcing a 300ms step in node time against an affected authbroker.

Mitigation options:
1) Immediate rollback of authbroker to v1.4.1 on the control plane — low-risk, restores previous behavior.
2) Apply a per-customer temporary config: increase allowed skew threshold to 500ms (safe but hides root cause).

I recommend option (1) for production stability. I've drafted a rollback playbook and a small evidence packet (rollback_plan_v1.4.3.pdf) with checks, verification steps, and a post-rollback artifact bundle we will deliver. I'll need a 1-hour maintenance window for the control-plane rollback and a short agent restart window (10–12 minutes) per node.

I'll coordinate with Michael and Lauren for scheduling; Cheng, can you confirm a preferred 1-hour window tomorrow? We'll also prepare the redwood_evidence_packet_20270517.zip after the rollback with logs and signed checksums for your procurement team.

-rishi
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

If that window works, we'll place the job and send a calendar invite with bridge details.

-mg

Subject: Post-rollback confirmation, evidence, and next steps

Cheng / Medsyn Ops —

Rollback completed at 02:47 PDT on 2027-05-17. Summary: authbroker was reverted to v1.4.1 across all control-plane nodes, agent restarts were staggered per the runbook, and we validated connectivity/health probes for 45 minutes post-rollback. Observed impact: two short reconnect windows during restarts (expected) but no spontaneous disconnects afterward.

Artifacts attached: redwood_evidence_packet_20270517.zip (signed checksums, node-level logs, and verification script). High-level postmortem points:
- Trigger: time-sync package on customer edge nodes exposed a bug in authbroker v1.4.2 token validation logic for >250ms skew.
- Immediate fix: rollback to v1.4.1 (completed).
- Medium-term fix: a patch (v1.4.3) with a time-sync guard and improved token revalidation will be published next week; we will coordinate a canary with Medsyn before general release.
- Compensation/credits: if you want us to start the SLA review now, we can calculate any impacted request volume and propose a credit; let us know.

Action items for Redwood (assigned):
- Rishi: publish v1.4.3 with guard and coordinate canary (ETA 2027-05-24).
- Neha: assemble evidence packet and hand to procurement (done).
- Michael: schedule follow-up call to review postmortem and the planned release.

Cheng: thanks for the quick capture and patience. We'll follow with the detailed postmortem doc and a separate implementation timetable for the patch.

Regards,
Michael Grant
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
